The current entry `zschache2026energy` in paper_final/references.bib (Scientific Reports, vol. 16, 12717, 2026, doi 10.1038/s41598-026-45023-0) matches the published record. arXiv 2508.14170 (Johannes Zschache, Tilman Hartwig, "Comparing energy consumption and accuracy in text classification inference"; v1 19 Aug 2025, v2 21 Apr 2026) lists the journal reference "Sci Rep 16, 12717 (2026)" and the related DOI https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-45023-0 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14170). The Crossref record of that DOI (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/s41598-026-45023-0) gives: title "Comparing energy consumption and accuracy in text classification inference", authors Johannes Zschache and Tilman Hartwig, Scientific Reports, volume 16, article number 12717, published online 17 April 2026, URL https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-45023-0 (the nature.com page itself redirects to a login wall for automated fetches and was not read). The bib field `pages = {12717}` holds the article number; the title in the bib uses title case, the published title is sentence case.

**What changes for the paper:** nothing; the citation can stay as it is.

verdicts.A1: The stratified bootstrap narrows every interval (StaticKD 0.501–0.585 instead of 0.490–0.605) because it treats the six sources as fixed and resamples the three single-cluster sources by documents; its inference is conditional on these sources and is a sensitivity analysis, not a replacement. No significance conclusion of the 14-comparison table changes at Holm 0.05: DistilmBERT stays non-significant (Holm p 0.136), MiniLM-L6 stays ahead (p<0.001), StaticKD-compact and TF-IDF + SVM + KD, which were borderline (p 0.042 and 0.040), become clear (p<0.001). The 512-token rows and the frozen ensemble keep their conclusions (frozen ensemble p 0.344 -> 0.059, still n.s.). The only changes are in the equivalence family: under the stratified bootstrap all eleven TOST claims survive Holm over 11 (Model2Vec 0.038, hard labels 0.006, tau=2 0.038), whereas under the paper's bootstrap these three do not (0.051). The paper's sentence that Holm raises the Model2Vec TOST p to 0.051 stays correct; it can add that the stratified bootstrap gives 0.038, but the equivalence should still be called borderline because it depends on how the sources are treated.
verdicts.A2: The mean of per-source macro-F1 keeps the ranking teacher (0.721) > MiniLM-L6 (0.684) > frozen ensemble (0.670) > StaticKD (0.661) > Model2Vec (0.654) > DistilmBERT (0.633), and every fastText, TF-IDF, SD-style and StaticKD-compact model is about 0.19–0.23 below StaticKD (all Holm p<0.001). StaticKD vs Model2Vec +0.006 [−0.002, +0.015], Holm p 0.364; vs MiniLM-L6 −0.024, Holm p 0.012; vs DistilmBERT +0.028, p 0.364. One claim weakens: on this metric the frozen-embedding ensemble scores significantly higher than StaticKD (−0.009 [−0.026, −0.002], unadjusted p 0.016), whereas the pooled test shows no significant difference. With the stratified bootstrap the restricted-inventory comparisons stay as in r4 (MiniLM lead not significant, Holm p 0.281; Model2Vec +0.008, p 0.057; DistilmBERT +0.023, p 0.064).
verdicts.A3: The calibration claim now has intervals: StaticKD ECE 0.041 [0.036, 0.070] on dev and 0.139 [0.122, 0.165] on test, the teacher 0.090 [0.072, 0.110] and 0.245 [0.212, 0.278]; the difference is −0.049 [−0.060, −0.016] (p 0.001) on dev and −0.106 [−0.139, −0.073] (p<0.001) on test (stratified: [−0.132, −0.079]). The claim that StaticKD is better calibrated than the teacher holds on both sets. Note that bootstrap ECE is biased upward on small resamples, which is why the dev point estimate lies near the lower end of its interval.
verdicts.A4: The reviewer's pattern is real but it is not caused by the LLM: on the 300 LLM-adjudicated audit labels the teacher-like models gain 3.5 pp more than fastText and TF-IDF (+9.5 vs +6.0 pp, [+0.8, +6.5], p 0.012), and on the 100 blind human-only labels the same gap appears (+13.6 vs +8.5 pp, difference +5.1 pp [+0.8, +10.0], p 0.022). On the audit labels the gap between StaticKD and the teacher widens from −5.7 to −9.0 pp (change −3.3 pp, p 0.064) and StaticKD falls significantly behind MiniLM-L6 (−4.3 pp, p 0.039; editorial −1.7 pp, p 0.417); on the human labels no paired difference of StaticKD is significant (teacher −3 pp, p 0.404). The paper can state that cleaner labels raise all models, raise the teacher-like models somewhat more, and that this also holds for human labels without any LLM step; the ranking teacher > MiniLM-L6 ≥ Model2Vec ≈ StaticKD > DistilmBERT > fastText ≈ TF-IDF is unchanged. The 100-article sample is small (Wilson intervals 13 to 18 pp wide).
verdicts.A5: Truncating StaticKD to 512 tokens changes nothing measurable: test macro-F1 0.545 (Δ +0.000 [−0.003, +0.004]), accuracy 0.640 (Δ −0.001), dev 0.759 (Δ −0.002, p 0.836), although 58.6% of the test articles exceed 512 tokens. At the same 512-token budget MiniLM-L6 stays significantly ahead (test −0.035 [−0.049, −0.020], Holm p<0.001) and DistilmBERT stays indistinguishable (−0.002, p 1.000). The comparison with the 512-token transformers is therefore not driven by StaticKD's longer input.
verdicts.A6: The teacher is more confident on its own fine-tuning data than on CC-News: on the 20,000 EMMediaTopic training articles mean max probability 0.970, 92.7% above 0.9, mean entropy 0.120 nats; on the 265,999 CC-News articles 0.938, 83.1% above 0.9, entropy 0.210 nats. The difference is tied to the corpus, not the language: CC-News articles in the four EMMediaTopic languages (25,467) give 0.941 / 83.7%, the other CC-News languages 0.938 / 83.0%. Medians are high everywhere (max probability 0.994–0.996), so most soft labels are close to one-hot; the EMMediaTopic part carries the least extra information beyond the arg-max label.
verdicts.A7: For a filtering use case StaticKD's confidence is usable: keeping predictions with max probability ≥ 0.9 retains 51.7% of the test articles at 83.9% precision (≥ 0.7: 67.4% at 78.8%), close to MiniLM-L6 (59.3% at 84.3%). The teacher keeps 85.1% at 76.3% because it is overconfident (A3). Weak labels stay weak for every model: society (F1 0.16), disaster (0.29), human interest (0.32) and conflict (0.37) have low precision; religion has low recall for StaticKD (0.34) and MiniLM-L6 (0.29) against 0.48 for the teacher. A compact supplementary table can be built from the per-label rows.
verdicts.A8: At the stored single-core speeds, 1 million articles per day need 0.021 cores for StaticKD, 0.68 for MiniLM-L6, 2.29 for DistilmBERT, 14.7 for the ONNX int8 teacher and 33.7 for the PyTorch teacher (as in the paper). 100 million per day need 2.15 StaticKD cores (3 processes × 501 MB ≈ 1.5 GB RAM) against 68 MiniLM-L6 cores, 229 DistilmBERT cores and 1,465 ONNX int8 teacher cores. The numbers assume 24 h at full load with no headroom and single-threaded processes.
verdicts.A9: The release manifest (dist/static_kd_iptc_classifier) gives the WARC file name for all 6,050 CC-NEWS articles plus the URL and a SHA-1 of the text, but no byte offset and no WARC-Record-ID; the extraction code (src/statickd/testset/jsonld.py) does not store them either, and the older dist/github manifest written by scripts/build_dist.py has no WARC field at all. Re-identification therefore requires scanning the named WARC file for the URL. The paper must not claim offsets or record IDs; code was not changed.
verdicts.B1: With n_layers=0 and every other library default (normalize=True) the Model2Vec classifier reaches 0.536 test macro-F1 (accuracy 0.625), 0.748 dev and 0.804 held-out agreement; StaticKD is +0.008 [−0.001, +0.016] ahead (p 0.077; stratified p 0.005) and the MLP-head default is +0.010 ahead (p 0.166). This model cannot be folded exactly: the library L2-normalises the pooled vector, so the logit is (sum of table rows) ÷ ||pooled 256-dim embedding|| + b and the norm needs the full embeddings. The fold is exact in that form (100% argmax agreement, max |Δlogit| 3e-5), but the plain 17-logit table without the norm agrees on only 96.1% of the test articles and scores 0.527. Trained with normalize=False (one extra change, needed for a 17-logit table), the linear head folds exactly into a 34 MB fp16 table that runs in the StaticKD inference code (99.98% test argmax agreement with the pipeline; the residual comes from the order of truncation and [UNK] removal in the two tokenisation paths) but scores 0.524 on test (StaticKD +0.021 [+0.003, +0.029], p 0.016) and 0.770 on dev (StaticKD −0.009, p 0.537). So a Model2Vec-trained table of exactly StaticKD's size and speed does not reach StaticKD on the independent test labels. Caveats: one seed per variant (the final recipe's seed SD is 0.004), unadjusted p, and the two training procedures differ in several settings at once (hard vs soft labels, learned token weights, early stopping, 512 vs 1,024 tokens).
verdicts.B1b: The B1 result holds across seeds. The three single seeds of the foldable linear-head Model2Vec classifier score 0.522 ± 0.002 test macro-F1 against 0.542 ± 0.004 for the ten single-seed runs of the StaticKD recipe (Δ +0.020 [+0.000, +0.029], paired-seed bootstrap p 0.049; Welch p<0.001), 0.606 vs 0.640 accuracy (+0.034, p 0.015) and 0.799 vs 0.808 held-out agreement (p<0.001); on dev they are level (0.760 vs 0.755, p 0.533). The folded 3-seed ensemble gains almost nothing over its members (test 0.525, accuracy 0.608, 87.7% of the teacher) and stays below the StaticKD ensemble: +0.020 [+0.002, +0.028], p 0.026 (stratified [+0.008, +0.027], p<0.001); accuracy +0.033, p 0.015; mean of per-source macro-F1 0.627 vs 0.661 (+0.034 [+0.016, +0.045], p<0.001); per-language mean 0.585 vs 0.622; dev 0.753 vs 0.761 (p 0.418). At identical format, size and inference code (34 MB fp16 table), StaticKD's training recipe therefore gives about 0.02 macro-F1 and 0.03 accuracy more on the independent test labels than a Model2Vec-trained linear head. The paper can state this as a same-format comparison; the remaining caveat is that the two training procedures differ in several settings at once (soft vs hard labels, learned token weights, early stopping, token dropout, 512 vs 1,024 tokens), so the gap cannot be attributed to one component, and the test p-values are unadjusted single comparisons.
verdicts.B2: Matching the size of the EMMediaTopic-only ablation (20,000 documents) but drawing the documents from CC-News in all 69 languages gives 0.533±0.001 test macro-F1 against 0.491±0.002 for EMMediaTopic only (+0.042 [+0.024, +0.057], p<0.001) and 0.542±0.004 for the full 285,999-document recipe (−0.009 [−0.019, +0.001], bootstrap p 0.092, not equivalent: TOST p 0.432; seed-level Welch p<0.001). About four fifths (82%) of the drop of the EMMediaTopic-only ablation on the test set is therefore due to language and source coverage rather than to the number of documents. The 20k multilingual model matches the full recipe in languages with few or no distillation data (0.482 and 0.406 vs 0.482 and 0.403) and trails it in well-covered languages (0.597 vs 0.615). Data size still matters for the in-distribution criteria: dev macro-F1 0.666 (full 0.755, EMMediaTopic-only 0.723) and held-out agreement 0.766 (full 0.808). The paper's reading of the emm_only ablation as a data-diversity effect is supported; it should not say that size is irrelevant.
verdicts.C: All speeds in this section come from one later session in which StaticKD ran at 474 articles/s on one core (paper table: 539) and the fp32 Model2Vec classifier at 525 (paper: 568); compare rows within this session, not with Table 9. (1) Model2Vec classifier: fp16 storage halves the file (507 -> 263 MB) and lowers model RAM from 1,091 to 847 MB with 1 changed prediction out of 12,744 and unchanged macro-F1 (0.547); int8 (model2vec's own global-scale quantization, saved and loaded through the pipeline, which has no quantize_to option) gives 140 MB and 723 MB RAM, 324 changed predictions and macro-F1 0.546 (Δ −0.000, p 0.792). Speed is unchanged on one core (499 and 504 vs 525 articles/s) and somewhat lower on four cores (1,460 and 1,591 vs 1,737). StaticKD still uses less RAM (501 MB) and a smaller file (34 MB); the paper's RAM/file comparison with Model2Vec should mention that the Model2Vec classifier's RAM can be cut to about 720–850 MB by storage precision without accuracy loss. (2) DistilmBERT int8 (teacher-style quantize_dynamic) keeps its accuracy (test 0.530 vs 0.534, Δ −0.005 [−0.008, −0.002]; still not different from StaticKD, Δ +0.015, p 0.684), runs 2.5× faster (11.9 vs 4.8 articles/s on one core, 41 vs 17 on four) and needs 677 instead of 1,060 MB RAM and 130 instead of 516 MB on disk; it remains about 40× slower than StaticKD. (3) MiniLM-L6 int8 with the same settings is 2× faster (30.8 vs 15.8 articles/s, 929 MB RAM, 102 MB) but collapses in accuracy (test 0.436 vs 0.565, Δ −0.129 [−0.151, −0.105]; StaticKD +0.109 ahead). The drop comes from quantizing the MatMul layers (MatMul-only 0.582 dev vs 0.783); quantizing only the embedding Gather keeps accuracy (dev 0.784, test 0.565, MiniLM still +0.020 ahead of StaticKD, p 0.002) but gives no speed-up (15.2 articles/s; 959 MB RAM, 133 MB file). Calibration-free dynamic int8 therefore narrows the speed gap only for DistilmBERT, and only by a factor of 2.5; the speed and RAM conclusions of the paper stand. The paper may state that int8 versions of the transformer students were tested and remain 15 times (MiniLM-L6, with the accuracy loss) to 40 times (DistilmBERT) slower than StaticKD on one core.
verdicts.C3_text: The exactly folded linear-head Model2Vec table (m2v_lin_nonorm_folded, B1) runs in the unchanged StaticKD inference code (spec `static:`) and has the same file size (34 MB), model RAM (503 vs 501 MB) and speed (493 vs 474 articles/s on one core, 1,738 vs 1,785 on four) as StaticKD in this session; it differs only in accuracy (test macro-F1 0.524 vs 0.545, B1). The normalised linear-head pipeline (m2v_lin) runs at 528 articles/s with 1,092 MB RAM and a 506 MB directory, like the MLP-head Model2Vec classifier.

Part B1 (GPU): 66 min 55 s wall in total; training 16.2 min (m2v_lin) and 33.1 min (m2v_lin_nonorm, slowed by RAM pressure: the process held about 8 GB), the rest is inference on three sets and the fold checks. Part B2 (GPU): 21 min 36 s wall; 22–26 s of training per seed, the rest is inference. Part C: quantization and accuracy evaluation 23 min 0 s, MiniLM quantization diagnostic 4 min 30 s, CPU benchmarks (11 configurations × 2 thread counts × 3 repetitions) 16 min 1 s. Benchmarks started only after the editor's EDITOR_DONE flag existed and with no other job of this task running; other desktop programs (VPN client, browser, IDE) were open as before and could not be closed by this task.
